clues: This town in the south of Italy lies between Bari and Foggia. It sits at the edge of a plateau that looks down on a wide valley.
Rain here falls mostly from autumn into spring, in the long stretch from September to April. The nearby hills shape how hot or cold each month feels.
After Rome lost a great battle nearby, its beaten soldiers found shelter by the river here. That old escape still marks the town's long past.
Old vases and other finds from digs fill its museums and private collections. Few towns in the land can match its deep, unbroken past.
This town is the burial place of Bohemund the First of Antioch. His tomb, resting here, is the clue that should settle the guess.
